description: Imports the records of every table in every Airtable base the credential can see, with each table's field schema discovered from the Airtable metadata API.

spec.apiVersionPinning: path segment `v0` baked into the base URL

configFields.name: credentials.auth_method
configFields.description: Discriminator; const `api_key` in the shipped schema, but auth.py also branches on the value `oauth2.0`.

configFields.name: credentials.client_id
configFields.description: Written by the OAuth flow (advanced_auth complete_oauth_server_output_specification); not present in connectionSpecification.

configFields.name: credentials.client_secret
configFields.description: Written by the OAuth flow; not present in connectionSpecification.

configFields.name: credentials.refresh_token
configFields.description: Written by the OAuth flow; rotated on every refresh (single-use).

configFields.name: credentials.token_expiry_date
configFields.description: Written by the OAuth flow as now + expires_in.

configFields.name: api_key
configFields.description: Undocumented legacy top-level path still honoured by auth.py before `credentials` is consulted.

configFields.name: syncMode
configFields.description: full_refresh | incremental (shim-provided; this connector only ever advertises full_refresh).

discovery.method: Airtable metadata REST API: list bases, then list tables per base; a JSON Schema is synthesised per table
discovery.querySketch: GET meta/bases (paginate) -> for each base id: GET meta/bases/{base_id}/tables -> emit one stream named `{base_name}/{table_name}/{table_id}` with path `{base_id}/{table_id}`
excludes: bases whose permissionLevel is "none" are skipped with a warning

pathPlaceholders.base_id: `id` of each base returned by the `bases` stream

authTierRationale: The only mode the shipped connectionSpecification advertises is a single self-serve Airtable Personal Access Token sent as a bearer token (`credentials.api_key`), which is T1_SIMPLE. The OAuth mode is T3_BYO_REFRESH standalone: `SingleUseRefreshTokenOauth2Authenticator` reads client_id, client_secret and a rotating refresh_token out of the config, and none of those appear in the user-facing config schema — they are populated by Estuary's hosted control plane, which registers the Airtable OAuth app on the user's behalf via the `oauth2` block in __main__.py. Standalone (no control plane) the user would have to register their own Airtable OAuth app and supply the refresh token themselves.

unionMisfits.description: The connector has two live auth branches in code but only one in its published schema. spec.json's connectionSpecification declares `credentials.auth_method` as `const: "api_key"`, yet auth.py branches on `auth_method == "oauth2.0"` and the OAuth-only fields (client_id/client_secret/access_token/refresh_token/token_expiry_date) exist only in `advanced_auth.oauth_config_specification` path_in_connector_config entries. A pure schema-driven reader would never discover the OAuth mode.

auth.py accepts a third, wholly undeclared shape: a top-level `api_key` (no `credentials` wrapper), checked before `credentials` and used to build a TokenAuthenticator. It is a legacy compatibility path with no schema entry at all.

`bases` and `tables` are real HTTP streams with real paths but are never offered as bindings — they exist solely to drive discovery. The schema has no way to mark a stream as internal/discovery-only, so they are listed here with `origin: static` and their paths intact; do not read them as capturable collections.

Set to snapshot_with_tombstone with only medium confidence. Every stream is full_refresh (schema_helpers hard-codes supported_sync_modes=[full_refresh]), and the estuary-cdk shim gives full-refresh bindings the standard delete-annotated document schema (the `if _meta.op == "d"` clause in the discover snapshot). But records here carry a real source-defined key (/_airtable_id) rather than the synthetic /_meta/row_id, so the effective behaviour is closer to a keyed re-upsert of the whole table each run than to a true tombstoned snapshot.
Airtable is a hosted spreadsheet-database reached over REST. `database` in the category enum implies a SQL transport, so `other` was chosen; neither is a clean fit.

This legacy connector is an Airbyte-CDK source (airbyte_cdk.HttpStream, ^0.52) run through estuary_cdk.shim_airbyte_cdk.CaptureShim, NOT a native estuary-cdk HTTPMixin connector. Consequences vs the separately-mined source-airtable-native: auth is resolved by airbyte_cdk's TokenAuthenticator / SingleUseRefreshTokenOauth2Authenticator rather than estuary_cdk TokenSource; there is no per-binding schedule concept at all; every stream is full_refresh only; and the per-table JSON Schema is degenerate (only _airtable_id/_airtable_created_time/_airtable_table_name are declared, with real columns left to Flow's schema inference). If the two connectors disagree on paginator or field typing, this one is the older mechanism.

Internal inconsistency in the source, not a schema misfit, but worth recording: AirtableStream sets the airbyte class attribute `primary_key = "id"` while the emitted documents contain no `id` field (the record id is renamed to `_airtable_id`), and schema_helpers separately declares source_defined_primary_key=[["_airtable_id"]]. The shim uses the source-defined key, so /_airtable_id is what actually lands; the `id` attribute is dead and misleading.

credentialModes[0].scheme.snippet:
if "api_key" in config:
            return TokenAuthenticator(token=(config or {}).get("api_key"))

discovery.excludes.snippet:
if base.get("permissionLevel") == "none":
                self.logger.warning(f"Skipping base `{base.get('name')}` with id `{base.get('id')}`: Not enough permissions...")

abstained.credentialModes[0].scheme.prefix: The bearer prefix is not written in this repository. `TokenAuthenticator(token=...)` comes from airbyte_cdk.sources.streams.http.requests_native_auth, which is a PyPI dependency (airbyte-cdk ^0.52) and is not vendored here, so the exact header name and `Bearer ` prefix could not be confirmed from source in scope. Recorded as `bearer` on the strength of the constructor name only.
abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultHeaders: No default headers are set anywhere in the connector; only the authenticator's Authorization header is added.
abstained.execution.defaultSchedule: Neither the connector nor shim_airbyte_cdk defines any interval, cron, or delay. Cadence is entirely a Flow task property outside this code.
abstained.streams[].schedules: Same as above — the Airbyte shim has no per-binding scheduling concept.
abstained.streams[].cursorField: schema_helpers advertises only full_refresh and never sets default_cursor_field, and no stream sends a since/modified filter parameter. There is no incremental leg to have a cursor.
abstained.streams[*].pull.snapshot.paginator.pageS: No page-size parameter is ever sent (request_params returns only `offset`). The effective page size is whatever the Airtable API defaults to; it is not encoded here.
abstained.streams[*].pull.snapshot.params: request_params is empty apart from the pagination token — no filterByFormula, view, fields, or cellFormat is set.
abstained.streams[2].name: Discovered source: the literal stream list depends on the customer's bases and tables. The entry is an archetype using the recommendedName template `<clean(base_name)>/<clean(table_name)>/<table_id>`.
abstained.execution.continuity: mode is poll over a stateless REST API; no server-side artifact is created and nothing accrues or expires on either side.
